Traupman 315

tandem

adverb · Wiktionary

at last, finally, at length

“At long last” is tandem aliquandō (Cic. Cat. 1.18, 2.1) or jam tandem. In a question tandem means “pray”, “then”: quid tandem?

Other words

  • dēmum — only then, not till then, at last

    adverb, after a word of time: tum dēmum, nunc dēmum · also used · classical · Liv. 40.22.4: tertiō dēmum diē; Tac. Agr. 3.1: nunc dēmum redit animus; Traupman 337 · Wiktionary

Examples

  • dīcenda tacenda locūtus tandem dormītum dīmittitur

    having said everything, fit to say or not, he is finally sent off to bedHor. Ep. 1.7.72–73

  • tertiō dēmum diē ad verticem perventum

    it was only on the third day that they finally reached the topLiv. 40.22.4

  • ut tandem aliquandō timēre dēsinam

    so that at long last I may stop being afraidCic. Cat. 1.18

  • nunc tandem

    now at lastTraupman 88

See also finally, then.
